record.original_question: For tree parking functions and mapping parking functions, what can be proved about displacement statistics, including the total displacement of all drivers and the individual displacement of the k-th driver, where displacement means the driving distance from a driver's preferred parking space to the space where that driver actually parks?

evidence.quote: (4) As for ordinary parking functions one could analyse important quantities for tree and mapping parking functions. E.g., the so-called total displacement (which is of particular interest in problems related to hashing algorithms), i.e., the total driving distance of the drivers, or individual displacements (the driving distance of the k-th driver) seem to lead to interesting questions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let T be a rooted labeled tree on the vertex set [n] = {1, 2, ..., n} with root r, oriented so that every edge points toward the root; equivalently, let M : [n] → [n] be a mapping whose functional digraph has vertex set [n] with an edge from i to M(i). Each vertex is regarded as a parking space.

A sequence (a_1, a_2, ..., a_n) ∈ [n]^n of preferences for n drivers defines a parking process as follows. Drivers arrive in order 1, 2, ..., n. Driver k first attempts to park at vertex a_k. If that vertex is occupied, the driver moves along the directed edge to the next vertex (the parent in the tree case, or M applied repeatedly in the mapping case) and tries again, continuing until either an empty space is found (in which case the driver parks there) or no further moves are possible (in which case the process fails). The sequence is called a tree parking function for T (respectively a mapping parking function for M) if all n drivers successfully park.

Define the displacement d_k of driver k to be the number of directed edges traversed by driver k from a_k to the vertex where driver k actually parks. Define the total displacement to be D = d_1 + d_2 + ... + d_n.

For tree parking functions and for mapping parking functions, establish exact and/or asymptotic results for the distribution of:
(a) the total displacement D, and
(b) the individual displacement d_k of the k-th driver,
taken over uniformly random parking functions (and, where appropriate, over uniformly random underlying tree or mapping). In particular, determine generating functions, mean, variance, and limiting distributions of these statistics as n → ∞.
artifact.category_tag: parking functions on trees and mappings
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a direction for further research on tree and mapping parking functions. Displacement statistics are well studied for classical parking functions (and for ℓ-interval parking functions in recent work), but the literature on tree/mapping parking functions has so far focused on enumeration, lucky-driver statistics, and parking-success probabilities rather than on displacement distributions. No source found resolves the displacement distribution problem in the tree/mapping setting, so the problem appears open.

status_evidence.title: Short survey of results and open problems for parking problems on random trees
status_evidence.snippet: the so-called total displacement ... or individual displacements ... seem to lead to interesting questions
status_evidence.claim: Displacement statistics for tree and mapping parking functions are listed as open directions.

status_evidence.title: Parking functions for trees and mappings
status_evidence.snippet: Parking functions for trees and mappings, focusing on enumeration and parking success.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational work on tree/mapping parking functions does not address displacement distributions.

status_evidence.title: Statistics on ℓ-interval parking functions
status_evidence.snippet: enumerates ℓ-interval parking functions with respect to statistics such as inversion, displacement, and major index
status_evidence.claim: Displacement is studied for classical/interval parking functions but not in the tree/mapping setting.
